abstract: Pancreatic cancer remains highly lethal, and reliable metabolic and molecular markers for risk stratification and prognosis are limited. We investigated potential associations between circulating metabolites and pancreatic cancer risk and further evaluated the biological and prognostic relevance of prioritized candidate genes. We assessed 233 circulating metabolites using two-sample Mendelian randomization. Gene annotation, polygenic prioritization, summary-data-based Mendelian randomization, and Bayesian colocalization were used to prioritize candidate genes. Transcriptomic, proteomic, pathway, survival, and single-cell analyses were integrated with experimental validation, including Western blotting, gene knockdown, colony formation, wound-healing, Transwell migration, and immunohistochemistry. Fifteen circulating metabolites showed nominal Mendelian randomization association signals with pancreatic cancer risk. The free cholesterol-to-total lipids ratio in large very-low-density lipoprotein and saturated fatty acids showed relatively consistent inverse association patterns across multiple methods, whereas several other lipid-related traits showed method-specific exploratory signals. Excision repair cross-complementation group 1 (ERCC1) was prioritized as a candidate for further biological investigation. Colocalization did not support a shared causal variant between ERCC1 expression and pancreatic cancer risk, suggesting that ERCC1 should not be interpreted as a genetically confirmed mediator. The observed ERCC1-related metabolite associations therefore remained hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of an established genetic or metabolic mechanism. ERCC1 expression was increased in pancreatic cancer tissues and selected pancreatic cancer cell lines, associated with poorer prognosis, and enriched in malignant epithelial and cancer-associated fibroblast compartments. ERCC1 knockdown reduced clonogenic growth and migratory phenotypes, and immunohistochemistry showed stronger ERCC1 staining in pancreatic cancer tissues than in adjacent normal tissues in three paired specimens. Additional exploratory evaluation of the Cox-weighted prognostic score showed variable predictive performance in CPTAC-PDC000270 and E-MTAB-6134, with 1-, 2-, and 3-year AUCs of 0.658, 0.731, and 0.627 and 0.610, 0.607, and 0.553, respectively. This integrative analysis highlights lipid-related metabolic traits and provided expression-based and preliminary functional evidence supporting further investigation of ERCC1 in pancreatic cancer. Further mechanistic studies and lipidomic validation are warranted.
key_points_ko: 233개 혈중 대사물질 분석을 통해 지질 관련 대사 특성과 췌장암 위험 간의 연관성을 확인했습니다.
ERCC1 유전자는 췌장암 조직 및 암세포주에서 높은 발현을 보였으며 불량한 예후와 연관되었습니다.
ERCC1 노크다운 실험 결과 암세포의 집락 형성(clonogenic growth) 및 이동 능력이 감소했습니다.
CPTAC 코호트에서 ERCC1 기반 예후 점수의 1년, 2년, 3년 AUC는 각각 0.658, 0.731, 0.627을 기록했습니다.
summary_ko: 본 연구는 233개의 혈중 대사물질을 대상으로 멘델 무작위 배정(Mendelian randomization) 분석 및 다중옴닉스(multi-omics) 통합 분석을 시행하여 췌장암 위험 및 예후 관련 요인을 조사했습니다. 연구진은 ERCC1(Excision repair cross-complementation group 1) 유전자를 주요 후보 유전자로 발굴했습니다. ERCC1 발현은 췌장암 조직에서 증가되어 있었으며 불량한 예후와 연관성을 보였습니다. 세포 실험에서 ERCC1 노크다운(knockdown) 시 암세포의 증식과 이동 능력이 감소함을 확인했습니다.
title: Exploratory mendelian randomization of circulating metabolites and multi-omics characterization of ERCC1 in pancreatic cancer
title_ko: 췌장암에서 혈중 대사물질의 탐색적 멘델 무작위 배정 분석 및 ERCC1의 다중옴닉스 특성 분석
